statement: Labour share (nonfarm business, 4-quarter average) in 2027 is >= 1 pp below 2025 (BLS Productivity & Costs, Q4 2027 release)
status_at_phase_end: Bloc A nonfarm-business labour share hit successive record lows in 2026 (52.8% in Q2 2026 per BLS, lowest since 1947); Q3 preliminary data imply a further decline. 2025 4-quarter baseline not yet extracted from the series (to compute at calibration).

items.summary: Q1 2026 preliminary Productivity & Costs: nonfarm-business labour share reported at 54.1%, then a record low, down 0.3 pp from Q4 2025 (54.4%), while productivity rose 2.9% y/y.
items.detail: Secondary report reading BLS series PRS85006173 from the 2026-05-07 release (Bloc A). Figure later superseded by revised data (see item 002); confidence lowered because the level differs from the BLS TED series.

items.summary: Bloc A statistics office: nonfarm-business labour share was 52.8% in Q2 2026, the lowest level since the series began in 1947 (post-war range typically 60-66%).
items.detail: BLS The Economics Daily 'Labor share at its lowest level, 52.8 percent, in second quarter 2026' (Bloc A), based on the 2026-09-03 revised Q2 release.

items.summary: Revised Q2 2026 release: nonfarm-business unit labour costs +1.2% (annualised) vs unit nonlabour payments +14.8%; real hourly compensation -3.3% annualised - consistent with a falling labour share.
items.detail: BLS Productivity and Costs, Second Quarter 2026, Revised (archived release prod2_09032026), Table 2.

items.summary: Q3 2026 preliminary release: nonfarm-business productivity +3.6% (annualised), unit labour costs -0.7% while unit nonlabour payments rose 5.2% - implying a further decline in labour share in Q3. Q2 figures revised (nonlabour payments +13.2%).
items.detail: BLS Productivity and Costs, Third Quarter 2026, Preliminary (2026-11-05), Table 2 (Bloc A). Labour-share level for Q3 not stated in release text; direction inferred from ULC vs nonlabour payments.

items.summary: No comparable quarterly labour-share series exists for Bloc B; the indicator relies on a single-jurisdiction source. Regional equivalents (annual national-accounts labour share) are needed.
items.detail: Known gap per methods §2.6: BLS series covers the Bloc A only; Bloc B NBS publishes no quarterly labour-share equivalent.
